source_name: Vijesti — Ekonomija section (largest independent Montenegrin daily/portal)
why_relevant: Montenegro's leading independent daily and news portal; its economy desk covers CBCG press conferences, bank results and consumer payment topics, and often carries figures given verbally by regulators/bank executives. Listed by the Media Ownership Monitor as a major outlet.

source_name: Pobjeda — oldest Montenegrin daily (economy desk)
why_relevant: Long-running daily, historically state-linked, with close access to institutional sources (CBCG, Ministry of Finance, Uprava prihoda). Carries interviews and press-conference reporting where payment/card/cash figures are first disclosed. Profiled by Media Ownership Monitor Montenegro.

source_name: Dan — daily newspaper (dan.co.me)
why_relevant: Third major Montenegrin daily; economy/crime-desk overlap makes it a carrier of ATM-fraud, cash-handling and bank-fee stories that indirectly reveal ATM and card-network facts not published statistically.

source_name: CdM (Cafe del Montenegro) — Ekonomija section
why_relevant: High-volume portal that systematically republishes CBCG communications in near-press-release form ('CBCG: Platni promet 2,46 milijardi eura', 'CBCG priprema platni sistem za instant plaćanja', cross-border payment cost findings). Effectively a fast, structured mirror of regulator statistics announcements — the single most machine-friendly local-media channel found for payment figures.

source_name: RTCG — Radio Televizija Crne Gore, Ekonomija section
why_relevant: National public broadcaster; economy desk covers CBCG and ECB payment/cash policy in Montenegrin, and broadcast interviews with regulators/bankers are transcribed onto the site. Public-service status makes it a durable archive.

source_name: MINA / MINA-Business — Montenegrin News Agency, economic wire
why_relevant: The only national news agency; MINA-Business is the upstream wire that Vijesti/Pobjeda/CdM republish. Found carrying explicit card statistics ('Povećao se broj transakcija upotrebom platnih kartica' — Q1 card transaction volume +23%, value +6% per CBCG). Collecting the agency reduces duplicate downstream noise and gives earliest timestamps.

source_name: MINA-Business English wire
why_relevant: English-language mirror of the Montenegrin agency's business wire — lets English-only downstream tooling pick up the same CBCG-sourced payment and card figures without translation loss.

source_name: Gradski.me / PG TV — Podgorica city portal & TV, economy desk
source_subtype: local TV/city news portal, economy vertical
why_relevant: Carried the most granular local card/cash dataset surfaced in this run: 81.5m card transactions in 2025 worth ~EUR 2bn, card payment count +~20% y/y, 5.5m cash transactions split into 3.6m deposits and 1.9m withdrawals — a level of breakdown that mirrors CBCG source data and is exactly the A4 target metric set.

source_name: Portal Analitika — Ekonomija
why_relevant: Established Montenegrin news portal with a dedicated economy desk; adds a second independent editorial read on CBCG and bank-sector announcements, useful for cross-checking figures quoted in press conferences.

source_name: Aktuelno.me — Ekonomija
source_subtype: online news portal with browsable archive
why_relevant: Montenegrin news portal with an economy vertical and an open archive index (/arhiva/ekonomija), which makes historical back-filling of payment/card coverage cheaper than on outlets without a browsable archive.

source_name: Standard.co.me — Ekonomija
why_relevant: Podgorica-based Standard Media outlet with an economy section; broadens the local-press net beyond the four largest outlets and occasionally carries bank-executive interviews.

source_name: eKapija Montenegro (me.ekapija.com)
why_relevant: Regional B2B business/investment portal with a Montenegro edition covering tenders, investments and corporate announcements — the channel where POS/ATM procurement, bank IT tenders and vendor contract news surface, which is adjacent intelligence the general press does not carry.

source_name: Inflacija.me — consumer prices & finance portal
why_relevant: Niche Montenegrin portal focused on prices, money and household finance; carries cash-holding and central-bank cash-policy items in Montenegrin (e.g. coverage of a central bank advising households to hold cash), which is a distinct cash-usage sentiment signal.

source_name: Media Ownership Monitor Montenegro
why_relevant: Independent register of Montenegrin media outlets with ownership, reach and financing profiles. Essential for scoring the credibility and independence of each media source in this cell (e.g. state vs private ownership of Pobjeda vs Vijesti) and for discovering outlets not yet on the list.

source_name: CBCG payment-statistics pages (upstream verification target for media claims)
why_relevant: Not a media source, but the primary series that every figure in this cell is quoting. Included as the mandatory verification anchor: any card/ATM/cash number scraped from Vijesti, CdM, MINA or Gradski should be reconciled against the CBCG payment-traffic and payment-system statistics pages before use.

source_name: MONSTAT news archive (statistical office press releases quoted by media)
why_relevant: The statistical office's news archive is the second upstream that Montenegrin media quote for household/ICT/e-commerce indicators touching on payment behaviour; useful for tracing a press figure back to its release date.

source_name: European Commission — Montenegro Enlargement Report (annual country report, SWD series)
why_relevant: The annual EC country report is the single most authoritative benchmarked assessment of Montenegro's payments/financial-services alignment; Chapter 4 (free movement of capital) and Chapter 9 (financial services) sections carry qualitative and some quantitative statements on payment-system modernisation, PSD2 transposition, SEPA and instant payments. 2025 edition identified as SWD(2025) 754.

source_name: EC Screening Report Montenegro — Chapter 4 Free Movement of Capital
why_relevant: Baseline structural description of Montenegro's payment/capital regime at screening (2013); useful as the historical benchmark against which later progress reports and closing benchmarks are measured.

source_name: Council of the EU / Accession Conference press releases on Montenegro chapter closures
why_relevant: Records the formal opening/closing of Chapter 4 and associated closing benchmarks — the regulatory milestones that drive payment-market modernisation deadlines. Chapter 4 provisionally closed December 2025.

source_name: EU4ME / eu.me — Montenegrin Government EU-integration portal, Chapter 4 page
why_relevant: Official Montenegrin-language pointer hub: names the negotiating working group (led by CBCG), lists chapter documents, national programmes and legislative milestones (e.g. Zakon o platnom prometu amendments aligned with PSD2). Excellent snowball node into government PDFs.

source_name: Program pristupanja Crne Gore EU (PPCG) 2025–2026 — Ministry of European Affairs
why_relevant: The national accession programme sets dated, forward-looking commitments per chapter, including payment-system legislation, SEPA and instant-payments deliverables — forward targets no domestic statistical publisher produces.

source_name: Government of Montenegro document repository (wapi.gov.me / gov.me) — Ministry of European Affairs chapter materials
why_relevant: Hosts the raw PDFs of negotiating-position drafts, working-group reports and accession-programme annexes surfaced by search (wapi.gov.me/download-preview/... links). Primary repository for Montenegrin-language accession documentation touching payments.

source_name: European Payments Council — Montenegro SEPA accession news & insights
why_relevant: The EPC is the scheme authority that assessed and admitted Montenegro to SEPA geographical scope (21 Nov 2024) and set the Operational Readiness Date (5 Oct 2025). Its insight pieces contain accession-assessment reasoning and market context unavailable domestically.
